hypothesis.name: Tensor-dimensionality gate on gradient ridges: ridges whose potential-field gradient tensor is near-2-D (strike-extended) are more likely to be unmapped faults than ridges produced by compact 3-D sources such as intrusions or vents
hypothesis.derivation: FFT gradient tensor of each field; magnetic arm through a Baranov/Gunn pseudogravity (vertical integration) so the tensor is the Marussi tensor of a gravity-like potential

mechanism: For a source-free potential field the gradient tensor is trace-free and, for a strictly 2-D (strike-extended) source, its intermediate eigenvalue vanishes and the corresponding eigenvector is the strike. The Pedersen-Rasmussen dimensionality indicator I = 27*e3^2 / (4*(-e2)^3) is therefore 0 for a pure 2-D source and 1 for an equidimensional 3-D source. We rank gradient ridges by the corroborated horizontal-gradient magnitude of both fields and multiply by (1-I) and by a strike-agreement factor, so compact bodies are down-weighted and strike-extended ridges are kept.
non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contacts, dikes, sills and intrusive centres are also strike-extended and produce the same near-2-D tensor signature; hydrothermal alteration haloes and survey levelling seams are the other named mimics. No tensor signature is proof of faulting.

holdout_dti.ci_method: percentile bootstrap of 3182 spatial blocks of 40x40 px over the pooled additive DTI contribution maps
holdout_dti.limitation: The holdout truth is the PUBLIC catalogue (60,988 px), a proxy for - not a copy of - the private new-fault test set. Its size is ~3-4x the test set implied by the registry calibration, so the holdout-optimal dot count is biased high and the dot count was chosen from the registry calibration instead. Absolute holdout DTI is not a leaderboard prediction.

detail.test: withheld fault segments agree in strike with the tensor field more often than random detected ridges do

confirmatory_strike_test.interpretation: FAILED. Withheld catalogue fault segments do not agree with the tensor strike more often than random detected ridges do; the direction is significantly reversed. The likely cause is circularity: the ridge azimuth and the tensor eigenvector are derived from the same field, so a strong ridge is self-consistent whether or not it is a fault. The near-2-D gate, not the strike gate, carries the measured signal.
